thresholds.meaning: (relative, absolute): a change is flagged when it exceeds both

highlights.title: Verdict accuracy unchanged: 110 right / 1 misleading / 0 wrong runs (checks 254 / 1 / 0).
highlights.detail: The one misleading run is again a sampling miss of 1 % loss on the lossy link (lab-netem-pr run 1: 0 of 118 settled packets lost). Issue, hint, status and exit counts per scenario are identical to campaign 3; no false positives (0 of 11,335 settled packets lost on clean links).

highlights.title: Lossy link (lab-netem-pr, 3 campaign + 10 extra runs):
highlights.detail: healthy and exit 0 in 13/13 (campaign 3: 12/13); no 'closed stream' or transfer_failed (campaign 3: 1; one upload now waited past the 8 s limit for its count, 11.0 s); concurrency throughput in 13/13 (was 11/13), 0.46-3.64 Mbps, 2 restarts; relay_compare ok 13/13 (as before); packet_loss 9/13 (was 11/13; misses at the expected sampling rate).

highlights.title: Fast-path concurrency is measured instead of quantized:
highlights.detail: lab direct 185-252 Mbps (was 156 in every run), relayed 74-81, real-world direct 213-330, relay-only 65-87 Mbps; the 'improvement' flags on 12 scenarios are this measurement fix.

highlights.title: Regression flag on rw-easy-to-ufw is the environment:
highlights.detail: download 134.5 -> 15.6 Mbps, concurrency 279.6 -> 15.2 Mbps, run 13.8 -> 22.3 s: runs 1-2 (and rw-symmetric-to-open run 1) got 13.7-15.6 Mbps Hetzner -> lab at 01:34-01:36 UTC, with this machine's load at 36-45 from other sessions; 9 re-runs at 01:57-02:00 ran at 131-148 Mbps (debug/rw-recheck). Same symptom in campaigns 1 and 3 with older code.

highlights.title: Same outcomes, RTT and throughput:
highlights.detail: final paths 51 direct / 42 relay / 0 failed, 0 connections lost, QUIC counters in 93/93; lab RTT/throughput unchanged; real-world numbers move with the route clusters; benches on this machine bound ~50-60 ms slower under load; 418.3 MB through the real relay, no drops.

highlights.title: New bug:
highlights.detail: concurrency requests cut off by a restart or the time limit are not cancelled on the wire (Endpoint::request_from resets only before the request is fully buffered), so their data keeps using the link: after run8's restart the cut-off requests took most of the uplink (0.46 Mbps counted of ~1.2 Mbps sent), and in 7 of 13 lossy runs cut-off requests reached the listener up to 3.9 s after the phase had ended.
